title: The Apparent Motion of the Universe
deck:
Motion is presented as an appearance produced by infinite relations
            between static geometric configurations, rather than the
            displacement of material substance.

concise.body:
Apparent Motion of the Universe

According to traditional physics and philosophy—with the exception of certain philosophical schools, such as Pre-Socratic ontology—motion is considered a real property inherent to matter.

However, according to TUGIA, this issue has not yet been resolved, as there is no official (academic) acceptance that motion is absolutely non-existent, being merely an apparent property produced by an infinite density of geometric elements that interact within Absolute Empty Space.

The Problem of Motion: Parmenides and Zeno

When addressing the property of the motion of bodies, the motion of matter, the Pre-Socratic philosophers Parmenides of Elea and his disciple Zeno were, without a doubt, those who came closest to the absolute truth regarding this fundamental question.

As long as we do not assume that the being of supposed substantiality, that the being of supposed materiality—and therefore, that the being of the supposed reality of the universe—is a mere illusion, is only an appearance, and is only the result of the interaction between immaterial and dimensionless geometric elements with other immaterial and dimensionless geometric elements, then all paths of reasoning will lead us to paradoxes and absurdities.

For Parmenides, being is what is, while non-being is not; thus, being is spatially infinite, partless, complete, full, and therefore, immutable.

Zeno's Arguments against Motion (Paradoxes?)

1st The Dichotomy Paradox: Imagine a body positioned at a point A that one wishes to move to a point B.

Thus, the body at point A, whatever its structural dimension, possesses no real and insurmountable structure; it does not need to move through an entire space corresponding to its own structural dimension, for there is no such minimum and indivisible space that the body must necessarily occupy at every change until it reaches position B. In truth, according to the logic of TUGIA’s geometry, for the aforementioned "change" of the body from its initial position A to its final position B—the body being merely an immaterial and static geometric form—what occurs is merely an infinite succession of "drawings" of the body, whatever the body may be, between position A and B in space, rather than a real movement from A to B in a time $\Delta T$, for time also does not exist, given that motion does not exist.

2nd The Achilles Paradox: Imagine a race between Achilles and a tortoise.

According to the structure of TUGIA’s Geometric Hypercontinuum—and therefore, of the infinite Apparent Realities of the same structural dimension—Achilles defeats the tortoise because, in any single Apparent Reality (such as our own, where Jesus Christ existed, where Hitler existed, and where you and I exist), the "physical laws" are exactly as we observe them, where the numerical, formal, and dimensional differences between the heavy and the light, the swift and the slow, the strong and the weak, and everything else that is antagonistic are exactly as we can attest.

3rd The Arrow Paradox: A flying arrow is at rest at any given instant.

4th The Stadium Paradox: Similar to the arrow at rest, it argues that it is impossible for the subdivisibility of time and space to end in indivisibles.

Motion from the Perspective of Physics

According to the relativistic formula of matter-energy equivalence, $E = mc^2$, matter "transforms" into energy and vice-versa.

However, according to the logic of TUGIA's Principle of Necessarily Indefinite Fragmentation, what would this energy actually be?

To physicists, motion is fundamentally different from energy; the motion of a body simply transports a quantity of energy that has been supplied to it.

Motion, according to physicists, can be understood as the variation of the spatial coordinates of a body relative to a reference frame, as a function of time, such that we have these two completely distinct properties: motion and time.

According to physics, the motion of bodies is absolutely real; it exists as a property inherent to bodies, which are supposedly constituted by matter—though the absolute concept of what matter truly is does not exist within that same science.

The propagation velocity of a photon in space corresponding to the interplanetary vacuum cannot be surpassed by any other particle existing in the universe.

Apparent Motion

All philosophical and physical dialectics regarding the constitution of the supposed universal materiality and its eventual possibility of motion, despite possessing the rational elements necessary for its comprehension, have been as if forgotten and dissolved amidst the many new scientific concepts that have emerged from the idea of a supposed origin of the universe.

For physicists, who have unduly seized this difficult philosophical task of unveiling the "secrets of the universe," there truly exists a "fundamental substance" in granular form, which they call "fundamental particles," moving through an absurd type of "space" that expands, shrinks, and even bends, forming the basis of an entire, unquestionable dynamic universal reality that supposedly emerged from non-reality itself, from "nothingness" itself, by means of a "Big Bang" some time ago.

What we have are merely "elements" that, in reality, do not "exist," for what cannot exist, from a logical and absolutely rational point of view, is precisely any type of "fundamental substance," such as that of the supposed "fundamental particles" chosen by physicists.

This question, in fact, gives rise to what appears to be a true paradox within this theory, since what exists is precisely what does not exist.

But does there not exist a universe, where we live and of which we are a part, which is totally dynamic and whose dynamics we cannot deny through our own sensory experiences?

Thus, every "motion" or every "action" between two or more bodies or systems of bodies is, in truth, merely the product of the "infinite static relations" between these infinite Static Geometric Snapshots that form the "apparent bodies," which constitute the Apparent Matter of the universe. Static Geometric Snapshots are "slightly" different from one another, as if they were the "static drawings" of each frame of a film reel, yet "static drawings" structured along the three Directions (3D) of this same Absolute Empty Space. We can exemplify this idea by drawing an analogy between the supposed "motion" of bodies in the universe and the Apparent Motions of characters and objects in a film, which result only from the projection of an "indefinite succession" of different "static drawings" onto the flat surface of a cinema screen, structured in only two Spatial Directions (2D).

By this analogy, we can say that this supposed "material reality" and this supposed "real motion" are, in fact, the product—not of a "projection," for there is no projector that projects a "3D film" with infinite Structural Dimension—but the product of the infinite "static relations" between the infinite "3D drawings" of absolutely all "apparent bodies" in the universe, in all their infinite Structural Dimensions, forming not a "2D screen," but a "3D volume," which is the "volume" of the Absolute and Dimensionless Empty Space where this entire film called Apparent Reality unfolds. The Static Geometric Snapshots forming this Apparent Reality are not formed by simple images, as if they were 2D photos recorded on a film strip, but are formed by Compalphas and Merons, which structure themselves through a hierarchical process into infinite Structural Dimensions, forming all types of molecules and, consequently, all types of "apparent bodies" of the universe. These Compalphas do not possess a minimum Structural Dimension; they do not have an insurmountable dimensional base like that of the supposed "fundamental particles" proclaimed by the physicists of the standard model.

In TUGIA, any of the infinite Structural Dimensions of Compalphas can be a "base dimension," and in any of them, these Compalphas connect through their Circles of Interaction and organize themselves adequately throughout the entire Absolute and Dimensionless Empty Space that is the universe, thus forming continuous geometric structures with infinite extension—that is, a structure where no part is separate from another, and which "fills" this Absolute Empty Space completely.

But since there exist infinite Geometric Continua of the same Structural Dimension, of infinite "arbitrary bases," superimposed at infinite positions of Absolute Empty Space, and since there exist infinite "distinct drawings" of each of the infinite "elements," we possess this necessary condition of "static relativization," which thus produces Apparent Motion and, therefore, an Apparent Reality.

The Attributes of Apparent Motion

Apparent Motion is the first intrinsic property of the element Apparent Matter and the third foundation of the universe.

I.

II.

Given dimensionless geometric elements as the generating principle of universal structures, how then can we explain the existence of the motion we perceive in these elements?

The motion of bodies, in TUGIA, can be defined as the apparent change in the spatial position of the infinite points that make up the different geometric elements (which macroscopically translate as bodies), along infinite parallel lines in a certain direction and sense.

The change is apparent, for all that exists are static geometries that change their positions only in an apparent manner. In other words, within the structure of the Geometric Hypercontinuum, a geometric fragment (a Compalpha, a Meron, etc.) can form infinite static geometric configurations throughout space—that is, they can form infinite static frames along infinite positions in space.

III.

In this geometric mechanism, whenever one axis changes its spatial position by value $\phi$, the other will also change with the same amplitude, but instantaneously, regardless of the distance separating them. This theory asserts that the velocity of Apparent Motion, because it is relative to each structural dimension of the Geometric Hypercontinuum, can be infinite.

TUGIA admits the existence of infinite velocities much greater than that of light throughout the infinite coexisting structural dimensions; the first immediately greater than that of light is the velocity of interaction between the "magnetic fields" of stars and planets—that is, of celestial bodies—which in TUGIA is called "High-Light" (Alta Luz). "High-Light" is a type of interaction that proceeds in a manner exactly equal to cyclic interaction, yet acting in a geometric structural dimension much larger than the Alpha Structural Dimension; it acts in the Epsilon Structural Dimension.

Another good example of infinite apparent velocity can be given. If we have a wheel of radius $R=1$ that rotates at any angle with any tangential velocity, a second wheel of radius $R=1/2$ connected to it will displace double the angle, with double the velocity of the first wheel. If a third wheel of radius $R=1/4$ is connected to the second, it will undergo angular displacement and velocity increase four times greater than the first wheel of the system in question, and if a fourth wheel of radius $R=1/8$ is connected to this third one, and to this another and another, ad infinitum, we will obviously have infinite angular displacement and infinite velocity increase.

IV.

full.body:
Apparent Motion of the Universe

According to traditional physics and philosophy—with the exception of certain philosophical schools, such as Pre-Socratic ontology—motion is considered a real property inherent to matter. Many of its aspects have already been exhaustively discussed and supposedly settled by various philosophical schools and by modern science as a whole, more precisely by physics.

However, according to TUGIA, this issue has not yet been resolved, as there is no official (academic) acceptance that motion is absolutely non-existent, being merely an apparent property produced by an infinite density of geometric elements that interact within Absolute Empty Space. We shall see that such geometry refers to a structural model whose basic building blocks are elements called Compalphas, the formers of what we understand as matter and energy.

The Problem of Motion: Parmenides and Zeno

When addressing the property of the motion of bodies, the motion of matter, the Pre-Socratic philosophers Parmenides of Elea and his disciple Zeno were, without a doubt, those who came closest to the absolute truth regarding this fundamental question. However, they erred when they established their logical arguments—perfectly rational, yet based on a material reality, a reality absolutely distinct from non-existence—which is why these arguments were perceived as paradoxes. Nevertheless, according to the Restrictive Problems of Reality and Logical Functionality of TUGIA, the fundamental problem—the problem from which all other issues related to the ideas of space, matter, motion, and time result—is solely related to the idea that something truly exists; it is related to the idea that there is a fundamental difference between being and non-being.

As long as we do not assume that the being of supposed substantiality, that the being of supposed materiality—and therefore, that the being of the supposed reality of the universe—is a mere illusion, is only an appearance, and is only the result of the interaction between immaterial and dimensionless geometric elements with other immaterial and dimensionless geometric elements, then all paths of reasoning will lead us to paradoxes and absurdities.

For Parmenides, being is what is, while non-being is not; thus, being is spatially infinite, partless, complete, full, and therefore, immutable. By asserting this, he claimed that change of any nature is unthinkable, and that, since motion is a change, it is impossible; for, in the final analysis, to move is to change, and to change is to cease to be and to pass into non-being in the same place. Zeno, the principal disciple and ardent defender of Parmenides' ideas, expanded his master's concepts—using analogies with people, animals, and things—to propose that motion does not exist. He achieved this through certain logical arguments that are erroneously known as paradoxes, and which to this day remain the focus of discussions among philosophers and scientists. These arguments are as follows:

Zeno's Arguments against Motion (Paradoxes?)

1st The Dichotomy Paradox: Imagine a body positioned at a point A that one wishes to move to a point B. Such motion is impossible, for before reaching point B, the body must reach the midpoint between A and B, that is, a point C. But to reach C, it must first reach the midpoint between A and C, namely a point D, and so on, ad infinitum. According to TUGIA’s Principle of Necessarily Indefinite Fragmentation, the dichotomy paradox ceases to be a paradox when we assume that there is no material reality for bodies, that they are constituted solely by geometric elements without any substantiality, and that their Structural Dimensions can be fragmented indefinitely, creating an opposite and infinite relationship between them. In TUGIA’s conceptual structure, from a logical standpoint, it is not space itself that can be fragmented indefinitely, for it is continuous and infinite; rather, what can be fragmented are only the Structural Dimensions of the immaterial geometric forms present within that space. It is these geometric forms that possess this property.

Thus, the body at point A, whatever its structural dimension, possesses no real and insurmountable structure; it does not need to move through an entire space corresponding to its own structural dimension, for there is no such minimum and indivisible space that the body must necessarily occupy at every change until it reaches position B. Instead, it can assume infinite intermediate spaces between A and B; that is, the infinite points constituting its form do not move from A to B, but are repeated infinitely between A and B. In truth, according to the logic of TUGIA’s geometry, for the aforementioned "change" of the body from its initial position A to its final position B—the body being merely an immaterial and static geometric form—what occurs is merely an infinite succession of "drawings" of the body, whatever the body may be, between position A and B in space, rather than a real movement from A to B in a time $\Delta T$, for time also does not exist, given that motion does not exist.

2nd The Achilles Paradox: Imagine a race between Achilles and a tortoise. Suppose the tortoise is given an initial head start. Achilles will never overtake it because when he arrives at the point from which the tortoise started, the tortoise will have already covered another distance; and when he reaches that mark again, the tortoise will have traveled another distance, and so on, ad infinitum. According to the logic of Apparent Motion as an infinite succession of drawings of an immaterial geometry, what we have here in this "paradox" is a cardinal geometric advantage that can never be balanced. The points composing the "drawing" of the tortoise already start ahead of the points composing the "drawing" of Achilles, and for every set of static points—for every new "static frame" of the relationship between the two characters—the tortoise will always be one infinitesimal "static frame" ahead of Achilles; therefore, Achilles will never defeat the tortoise.

According to the structure of TUGIA’s Geometric Hypercontinuum—and therefore, of the infinite Apparent Realities of the same structural dimension—Achilles defeats the tortoise because, in any single Apparent Reality (such as our own, where Jesus Christ existed, where Hitler existed, and where you and I exist), the "physical laws" are exactly as we observe them, where the numerical, formal, and dimensional differences between the heavy and the light, the swift and the slow, the strong and the weak, and everything else that is antagonistic are exactly as we can attest. There exist, therefore, other infinite Apparent Realities where infinite laws exist in ways different from our own. It is through these infinite relations between the geometric forms constituting the bodies, in any of the infinite Apparent Realities, that living creatures and thinking beings can realize that motion exists—that is, Apparent Motion. And it is from the relation between the different intensities of the Apparent Motions of bodies that we derive the notion of time, or rather, Apparent Time.

3rd The Arrow Paradox: A flying arrow is at rest at any given instant. Now, if an object is at rest when it occupies a space equal to its own dimensions, and if the flying arrow always occupies a space equal to its own dimensions, then the flying arrow is at rest. This argument of Zeno, like all the others—principally that of the stadium (of opposing darts)—are not paradoxes once we understand that space can truly be fractionated indefinitely, that motion does not fundamentally exist, and that time is merely a function of the relationship between different intensities or measures of an illusory movement, of an Apparent Motion.

4th The Stadium Paradox: Similar to the arrow at rest, it argues that it is impossible for the subdivisibility of time and space to end in indivisibles.

Motion from the Perspective of Physics

According to the relativistic formula of matter-energy equivalence, $E = mc^2$, matter "transforms" into energy and vice-versa. This leads us to suppose, in the ultimate instance of materiality, that if a fundamental particle, such as a quark or an electron, were accelerated to the speed of light, it would be completely "converted" into energy—the purest energy—with the result of this hypothetical process being the very concept of energy itself.

However, according to the logic of TUGIA's Principle of Necessarily Indefinite Fragmentation, what would this energy actually be? Would it be the absolute pulverization or the absolute dilution of the mass of the "particles" throughout space as a consequence of their acceleration? Is decreasing the size of these "particles" not merely another vicious circle generated by the inability to solve this ontological problem?

To physicists, motion is fundamentally different from energy; the motion of a body simply transports a quantity of energy that has been supplied to it. Bodies would merely be carriers of energy, like "freight trains," which at times would carry more or less energy. Through this conventional physical description, we can never form the idea that motion, in itself, could be the same thing as energy, in itself, as an inseparable unit.

Motion, according to physicists, can be understood as the variation of the spatial coordinates of a body relative to a reference frame, as a function of time, such that we have these two completely distinct properties: motion and time. There are many types of motion, for example, accelerated motion; motion in which acceleration is non-zero, whether positive or negative; rotational motion, which a body performs around a point situated within its trajectory, etc. Regardless of the type, it is all merely motion.

According to physics, the motion of bodies is absolutely real; it exists as a property inherent to bodies, which are supposedly constituted by matter—though the absolute concept of what matter truly is does not exist within that same science. According to physicists, the highest possible velocity in the universe is the speed of light.

The propagation velocity of a photon in space corresponding to the interplanetary vacuum cannot be surpassed by any other particle existing in the universe. Yet, they admit that, at the supposed initial moment of the universe, during the Big Bang, primordial matter was accelerated to a velocity much higher (and indeterminate) than the speed of light of current times. This leads us to question whether the laws of the universe have changed over time. Is the universe becoming old and tired, as if it were an old man?

Apparent Motion

All philosophical and physical dialectics regarding the constitution of the supposed universal materiality and its eventual possibility of motion, despite possessing the rational elements necessary for its comprehension, have been as if forgotten and dissolved amidst the many new scientific concepts that have emerged from the idea of a supposed origin of the universe. Yet, the universe is infinite in every aspect! Thus, the search for the understanding of these "universal infinities" has never been, and never will be, a task for physicists, whose instruments—with their insignificances and limitations imposed by their rulers and clocks—are inadequate; rather, it is a task destined exclusively for philosophers, whose instruments of synthesis and analysis of acquired information are the shapers of new ideas, and are backed by logic and reason. Therefore, reason is the guide of experience, and not the reverse.

For physicists, who have unduly seized this difficult philosophical task of unveiling the "secrets of the universe," there truly exists a "fundamental substance" in granular form, which they call "fundamental particles," moving through an absurd type of "space" that expands, shrinks, and even bends, forming the basis of an entire, unquestionable dynamic universal reality that supposedly emerged from non-reality itself, from "nothingness" itself, by means of a "Big Bang" some time ago. However, according to the logical and axiomatic propositions of the Theory of the Universe of Immaterial and Dimensionless Geometry (TUGIA), the universe is simply infinite in every aspect; therefore, it did not "emerge" from an "infinite nothing," nor was it "created" by something or "someone" necessarily contained by this same "infinite nothing." Consequently, its "structures" are not substantial; they are not material, for they are formed only by "absolutely static immaterial and dimensionless geometric elements," superimposed within the Absolute and Dimensionless Empty Space that is "our" universe.

What we have are merely "elements" that, in reality, do not "exist," for what cannot exist, from a logical and absolutely rational point of view, is precisely any type of "fundamental substance," such as that of the supposed "fundamental particles" chosen by physicists. Thus, if there are no "fundamental particles" arranged in space constituting all bodies, there is no reason for "motion" to exist. How, then, can one say, from a logical, rational, and linguistic point of view, that what "exists in motion" is precisely a "motionless non-existence"?

This question, in fact, gives rise to what appears to be a true paradox within this theory, since what exists is precisely what does not exist. However, there is no paradox at all, for both the Absolute Empty Space and the "immaterial geometric elements" contained within it do not "exist," since points, lines, planes, and geometric solids are not "made" of a "fundamental substance," both being the same "nothing." Therefore, in this absolute non-existence, formed by the Absolute Empty Space and the "immaterial geometric elements"—in this infinite "Non-being"—there is no reason for "motion" to exist; for if the universe is an "infinite nothing," there is nothing to "move" or nothing to "be moved."

But does there not exist a universe, where we live and of which we are a part, which is totally dynamic and whose dynamics we cannot deny through our own sensory experiences? Yes, it exists, but according to TUGIA, both the supposed universal substantiality and its supposed "mobility" are merely "appearances"; they do not exist in fact, since this "apparent substance," called Apparent Matter in the context of TUGIA, is formed by infinite "static and immaterial geometric elements"—it is formed by infinite "static and immaterial drawings." Its supposed "motions" are merely the product of infinite "static relations" between each of these infinite "static immaterial drawings," thus forming the Apparent Motion of TUGIA. According to TUGIA, the supposed "real motion" of supposed "real bodies" is nothing more than Apparent Motion; it is nothing more than the product of the "infinite static relations" that exist between the "infinite static immaterial drawings," which we may call Static Geometric Snapshots. The infinite superpositions of these Infinite Static Geometric Snapshots, distinctly structured at infinite positions in the Absolute and Dimensionless Empty Space, in a single "time," all at once, form infinite Apparent Realities that are absolutely static, in which there can be no "past" or "future," but only an "eternal present."

Thus, every "motion" or every "action" between two or more bodies or systems of bodies is, in truth, merely the product of the "infinite static relations" between these infinite Static Geometric Snapshots that form the "apparent bodies," which constitute the Apparent Matter of the universe. Static Geometric Snapshots are "slightly" different from one another, as if they were the "static drawings" of each frame of a film reel, yet "static drawings" structured along the three Directions (3D) of this same Absolute Empty Space. We can exemplify this idea by drawing an analogy between the supposed "motion" of bodies in the universe and the Apparent Motions of characters and objects in a film, which result only from the projection of an "indefinite succession" of different "static drawings" onto the flat surface of a cinema screen, structured in only two Spatial Directions (2D).

By this analogy, we can say that this supposed "material reality" and this supposed "real motion" are, in fact, the product—not of a "projection," for there is no projector that projects a "3D film" with infinite Structural Dimension—but the product of the infinite "static relations" between the infinite "3D drawings" of absolutely all "apparent bodies" in the universe, in all their infinite Structural Dimensions, forming not a "2D screen," but a "3D volume," which is the "volume" of the Absolute and Dimensionless Empty Space where this entire film called Apparent Reality unfolds. The Static Geometric Snapshots forming this Apparent Reality are not formed by simple images, as if they were 2D photos recorded on a film strip, but are formed by Compalphas and Merons, which structure themselves through a hierarchical process into infinite Structural Dimensions, forming all types of molecules and, consequently, all types of "apparent bodies" of the universe. These Compalphas do not possess a minimum Structural Dimension; they do not have an insurmountable dimensional base like that of the supposed "fundamental particles" proclaimed by the physicists of the standard model.

In TUGIA, any of the infinite Structural Dimensions of Compalphas can be a "base dimension," and in any of them, these Compalphas connect through their Circles of Interaction and organize themselves adequately throughout the entire Absolute and Dimensionless Empty Space that is the universe, thus forming continuous geometric structures with infinite extension—that is, a structure where no part is separate from another, and which "fills" this Absolute Empty Space completely. These immaterial and dimensionless geometric structures, formed by the infinite Structural Dimensions of Compalphas, are called Geometric Continua. However, a single Geometric Continuum is not capable of enabling a relativization of its parts, since this continuous and infinite structure is immaterial and motionless, like a "continuous and infinite drawing" made with a single stroke, drawn with a single line; therefore, it is not capable of producing Apparent Motion or an Apparent Reality. It is necessary, therefore, that there be no fewer than infinite "copies" of each of the infinite "elements" of each Geometric Continuum, thus enabling their infinite "static relations," which is impossible when dealing with only a single Geometric Continuum.

But since there exist infinite Geometric Continua of the same Structural Dimension, of infinite "arbitrary bases," superimposed at infinite positions of Absolute Empty Space, and since there exist infinite "distinct drawings" of each of the infinite "elements," we possess this necessary condition of "static relativization," which thus produces Apparent Motion and, therefore, an Apparent Reality. This infinity of distinct Geometric Continua, superimposed at the same place in Absolute Empty Space, form other structures which are called, in TUGIA, Geometric Hypercontinua. These structures, ultimately, characterize themselves as the supposed "material reality" that we perceive and cannot deny. It is through the relativization of its components that all "apparent bodies" cause an impression (of a purely geometric order) upon one another, and from there, in a very high degree of complexity and dimension, upon the sense organs, such as an eye, for example. For such organs, in truth, are also products of geometric structures (fragments of this relational geometry), only much more complex than a simple geometric fragment forming a "matter particle" of mineral or organic origin without specific utility.

The Attributes of Apparent Motion

Apparent Motion is the first intrinsic property of the element Apparent Matter and the third foundation of the universe. Its attributes are defined by the following four postulates:

I. Motion is apparent; in principle, it does not exist, for since there is nothing to move, there is nothing to manifest such a property. A Geometric Snapshot can be understood as a drawing—the geometric trace produced by Compalphas within the structure of the Geometric Hypercontinua. Thus, the motion of a Metalpha Meron (hydrogen) from position A to B, for example, can be understood as a succession of infinite "photos" of this Meron distributed along the space AB, with this effect applying to all bodies.

II. Apparent Motion is relative; for it depends on the relationship of infinite distinct Geometric Snapshots to exist, and it is relative regarding its possible intensities, each being the product of the relationship of one quantity of Apparent Motion to another quantity of Apparent Motion. The intensity of Apparent Motion can only be measured if relativized against the speed of another Apparent Motion performed by another system, such as a measuring device, when we relate it to the velocity of the Apparent Motion of another system. Thus, we can say that a velocity of Apparent Motion (arbitrary) "performed" by a geometric point (a system) displacing itself from A to B can, relative to another system, be considered infinitely slow (yet without ever ceasing to be Apparent Motion) or infinitely fast.

Given dimensionless geometric elements as the generating principle of universal structures, how then can we explain the existence of the motion we perceive in these elements? The Earth rotates on its axis, revolves around the sun, revolves around the galactic center, and possesses a movement of recession in a certain direction relative to a fixed point in absolute spatial coordinates; however, this is due to random expansions of regions of the universe and not to expansion produced by a supposed Big Bang. In truth, motion does not exist. What exist are infinite possibilities for each of the infinite geometric elements constituting the Geometric Hypercontinuum to assume infinite relative positions among themselves, and to be in any of the infinite positions of Absolute Space.

The motion of bodies, in TUGIA, can be defined as the apparent change in the spatial position of the infinite points that make up the different geometric elements (which macroscopically translate as bodies), along infinite parallel lines in a certain direction and sense. However, it can simply be defined as the apparent change in the spatial position of a single point along a single line in a certain direction and sense. Thus, the question resides in the definition of apparent change. Apparent change is so named because the points of Immaterial Geometry do not actually change their spatial positions, since along a finite line segment there exist infinite points, not a single special point. Thus, any point may be in one position and any other point in another, forming an ordered system of points that, relative to another ordered system of points, appears cardinally larger or smaller. If the two systems are relativized, one of them will appear either (infinitely) larger or (infinitely) smaller.

The change is apparent, for all that exists are static geometries that change their positions only in an apparent manner. An example of static geometry is the case of two points along a line segment; therein, infinite points can exist separated by arbitrary distances. If a standard (also arbitrary) reference of lengths does not exist, any two points can be separated by any distance. If we create an infinite relation of distances between any two points on a line segment and two other fixed points, on the same or a parallel segment, we obtain values that can be cardinally larger or smaller to infinity. In other words, within the structure of the Geometric Hypercontinuum, a geometric fragment (a Compalpha, a Meron, etc.) can form infinite static geometric configurations throughout space—that is, they can form infinite static frames along infinite positions in space. The set of coordinates defining each point of a particular geometric architecture can assume infinite positions in space, whether or not it keeps such configuration intact. Thus, each of the infinite odd static frames, when related to other arbitrary frames, may or may not have morphological alterations. Such alterations produce the notion of motion. Keeping this in mind, we cannot accept the idea of motion.

III. Apparent Motion has infinite velocity; In the process of geometric interaction—which, when within the structure of the Geometric Continuum, is called cyclic interaction—two external tangent axes of a circle of radius R, which are equidistant from the center, when undergoing symmetric angular change defined by $\phi$ (theta), also modify the angle of the segments of half-lines perpendicular to them by the same angle. The symmetric projections of the half-line segments intersect at half the distance separating the two points. For each value of the displacement angle of the axes, there are identical values for the half-line segments. Thus, for each new displacement angle, there is a different value for the length of the half-lines, and associated with each value is a new radius value for the Circle in question.

In this geometric mechanism, whenever one axis changes its spatial position by value $\phi$, the other will also change with the same amplitude, but instantaneously, regardless of the distance separating them. As we can see, if this geometric interaction can be dimensionless, it can "transmit" information instantaneously, whatever the distance between the points generating and receiving this information. The concept of "transmitting," in this case, cannot be used adequately, for when we say "transmit" something, we suppose that the "something" has an origin and a destination in space and time—that is, it goes from one point to another over a certain time. This theory asserts that the velocity of Apparent Motion, because it is relative to each structural dimension of the Geometric Hypercontinuum, can be infinite. Therefore, the speed of light, in TUGIA, is merely a speed limit imposed by only one of the infinite structural dimensions of the Geometric Hypercontinua.

TUGIA admits the existence of infinite velocities much greater than that of light throughout the infinite coexisting structural dimensions; the first immediately greater than that of light is the velocity of interaction between the "magnetic fields" of stars and planets—that is, of celestial bodies—which in TUGIA is called "High-Light" (Alta Luz). This type of interaction acts significantly between bodies of great dimension, for example, between stars and between stars and planets; however, small bodies can also undergo atuação (action/influence) capable of being measured. Perhaps this type of interaction can be used for quasi-instantaneous communication within solar systems like ours, for in relation to the speed of light, it is a practically instantaneous interaction within the dimensions of these systems. "High-Light" is a type of interaction that proceeds in a manner exactly equal to cyclic interaction, yet acting in a geometric structural dimension much larger than the Alpha Structural Dimension; it acts in the Epsilon Structural Dimension.

Another good example of infinite apparent velocity can be given. Let us imagine a system of wheels constituted by circumferences of Immaterial Geometry—that is, by geometric elements that are "nothing." In this system, any wheel C, if we convention that they possess rotational movements, always touches another that possesses half its dimension, immediately at any point on its perimeter; thus, they act like gears. Each wheel of this hypothetical system can be infinitely larger or smaller when correlated. If we have a wheel of radius $R=1$ that rotates at any angle with any tangential velocity, a second wheel of radius $R=1/2$ connected to it will displace double the angle, with double the velocity of the first wheel. If a third wheel of radius $R=1/4$ is connected to the second, it will undergo angular displacement and velocity increase four times greater than the first wheel of the system in question, and if a fourth wheel of radius $R=1/8$ is connected to this third one, and to this another and another, ad infinitum, we will obviously have infinite angular displacement and infinite velocity increase. It is obvious that we can fractionate the radii of subsequent wheels to infinity in relation to the original one. Thus, when the first pulley rotates at any angle and at any velocity, the pulley infinitely smaller than it will perform infinite rotations with an apparent velocity that is also infinite.

IV. Apparent Motion is the generator of Apparent Time; for every notion of time we have is uniquely and exclusively due to motion, in this case, an Apparent Motion. The clearest idea we have of the passage of time is the passing of days and nights here on Earth—that is, the rotation movement of the Earth around its axis. If it were not for this, we would likely have no notion of time at all. We would not see stars passing through the celestial vault, nor the sun or moon; it would be like looking at an absolutely static photograph of the sky.
